fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. "…the terror of the LORD had fallen upon them." That's why Judah attacked all the cities around Gerar and plundered them, since there was much plunder there (2 Chronicles 14:14). I'd say that's a whole lot of fear landing at once.

Yes, friend. Asa, the new king of Judah, did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God (2 Chronicles 14:2). That's how the writer sums him up before telling us what he did. Most of us would need a few extra paragraphs to explain ourselves.

Interesting pick, friend, but priestly isn't in the verse. Asa built fortified cities in Judah while the land was at peace (2 Chronicles 14:6). Then he talks about walls, towers, doors and bars (2 Chronicles 14:7). That's a city with its apron tied on tight, ready for whatever comes.

You got it, baker. "…the LORD had given him rest." Asa says the same thing to the people: "…He has given us rest on every side." (2 Chronicles 14:7). Rest is a gift here, and the text says who gave it. That's the kind of gift I'd happily unwrap twice.

Good word, baker, but not the one in this verse. Verse 6 says the LORD had given him rest, and that's why no one made war with him. Asa says it again to the people: "…He has given us rest on every side." (2 Chronicles 14:7). Wisdom is wonderful, but I'd say rest is the gift that lets a kingdom sleep in.

Exactly, baker. "Then Asa cried out to the LORD his God…" He has marched out and lined up in battle formation, and a million men are in front of him. Right there in the valley, he prays. That's a good lesson for me, because at a hard moment I'm more likely to stare at the ceiling.

Not this time, friend. The text says the Cushites "…fell and could not recover, for they were crushed before the LORD and His army." They don't come back for another round. After the chase to Gerar, the text turns to Judah's plunder.
